<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S5.SS4" title="In 5 Experiments ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">5.4 </span>Ablation: V-Channel Saturation</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S5.SS5" title="In 5 Experiments ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">5.5 </span>Value-Space Profiling</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S5.SS6" title="In 5 Experiments ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">5.6 </span>Qualitative Comparison</span></a></li>
</ol></li>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line ltx_pruned_first">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Guandong Li
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>iFLYTEK
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">(Corresponding Author)
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Mengxia Ye
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Aegon THTF
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Training-free control over editing intensity is a critical requirement for diffusion-based image editing models built on the Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architecture. Existing attention manipulation methods focus exclusively on the Key space to modulate attention routing, leaving the Value space—which governs feature aggregation—entirely unexploited. In this paper, we first reveal that both Key and Value projections in DiT’s multi-modal attention layers exhibit a pronounced <em id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">bias-delta</em> structure, where token embeddings cluster tightly around a layer-specific bias vector. Building on this observation, we propose <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dual-Channel Attention Guidance (DCAG)</span>, a training-free framework that simultaneously manipulates both the Key channel (controlling <em id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">where</em> to attend) and the Value channel (controlling <em id="abstract1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">what</em> to aggregate). We provide a theoretical analysis showing that the Key channel operates through the nonlinear softmax function, acting as a coarse control knob, while the Value channel operates through linear weighted summation, serving as a fine-grained complement. Together, the two-dimensional parameter space <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})</annotation></semantics></math> enables more precise editing-fidelity trade-offs than any single-channel method. Extensive experiments on the PIE-Bench benchmark (700 images, 10 editing categories) demonstrate that DCAG consistently outperforms Key-only guidance across all fidelity metrics, with the most significant improvements observed in localized editing tasks such as object deletion (<math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>4.9% LPIPS) and object addition (<math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>3.2% LPIPS).</p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="p1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></p>
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent advances in Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite> have enabled powerful instruction-guided image editing models such as Qwen-Image-Edit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite> and Step1X-Edit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>. These models accept a source image and a natural language editing instruction, producing an edited image that faithfully follows the instruction while preserving unrelated content. However, a fundamental challenge remains: <em id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">how to precisely control the trade-off between editing strength and content preservation without additional training</em>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite> provides a basic mechanism for adjusting generation strength, but its control over editing intensity is coarse and often leads to artifacts at extreme scales. More recently, attention manipulation methods have emerged as a promising direction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>, <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>. GRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite> decomposes the Key projections in multi-modal attention layers into a bias and delta component, then rescales them to control editing intensity. While effective, GRAG and similar approaches operate exclusively on the Key space, which governs <em id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">attention routing</em>—determining which tokens receive attention. The Value space, which controls <em id="S1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">what content is aggregated</em> after attention weights are computed, remains entirely unexploited.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we make the following key observation: the bias-delta structure is not unique to Keys. <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Value projections in DiT’s multi-modal attention layers exhibit the same pronounced clustering phenomenon</span>, where all token embeddings concentrate around a layer-specific bias vector. This suggests that the Value space offers an independent, orthogonal channel for editing control.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Building on this observation, we propose <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dual-Channel Attention Guidance (DCAG)</span>, a training-free framework that simultaneously manipulates both the Key and Value channels. The attention output in a transformer layer can be decomposed as:</p>
<table id="S1.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\text{Output}=\underbrace{\text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^{\top}}{\sqrt{d}}\right)}_{\text{K: attention routing}}\cdot\underbrace{V}_{\text{V: feature aggregation}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>Output</mtext><mo>=</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mtext>softmax</mtext></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mo rspace="0.055em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>K: attention routing</mtext></msub><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>V: feature aggregation</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Output}=\underbrace{\text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^{\top}}{\sqrt{d}}\right)}_{\text{K: attention routing}}\cdot\underbrace{V}_{\text{V: feature aggregation}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">DCAG applies bias-delta rescaling to both <math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math>, creating a two-dimensional parameter space <math id="S1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})</annotation></semantics></math> that enables finer-grained control than any single-channel method. We provide a theoretical analysis revealing that the two channels have fundamentally different control characteristics: the Key channel operates through the nonlinear softmax function, where small perturbations are exponentially amplified (coarse control), while the Value channel operates through linear weighted summation, producing proportional and predictable effects (fine control).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Our contributions are summarized as follows:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We discover that both Key and Value spaces in DiT’s multi-modal attention exhibit a bias-delta structure, revealing the Value space as an overlooked control channel for editing guidance.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide a theoretical analysis of the distinct control characteristics of the Key channel (nonlinear, dominant) and Value channel (linear, complementary), explaining their orthogonal roles.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose DCAG, a unified dual-channel framework with a 2D parameter space <math id="S1.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})</annotation></semantics></math> that subsumes single-channel methods as special cases.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct extensive experiments on PIE-Bench, demonstrating consistent improvements over Key-only guidance across 8 out of 10 editing categories, with up to 4.9% LPIPS reduction in localized editing tasks.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training-Free Editing Control.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Controlling the intensity of image edits without retraining is a long-standing challenge. Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite> adjusts the balance between conditional and unconditional predictions during sampling, but provides only coarse control over editing strength <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>. SDEdit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> controls editing intensity through the noise level added to the source image, but conflates structural changes with detail preservation. Null-text Inversion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite> enables faithful reconstruction via DDIM inversion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite> for subsequent editing, while Plug-and-Play <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> leverages diffusion features for image-to-image translation. InstructPix2Pix <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite> trains an end-to-end model for instruction-based editing, and Imagic <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite> optimizes text embeddings for real image editing. FlowEdit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite> and related flow-based methods <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>, <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite> offer alternative control mechanisms but require careful tuning of multiple hyperparameters. In contrast, our approach operates directly within the attention mechanism, providing interpretable and orthogonal control through two distinct channels.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Attention Manipulation for Image Editing.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Manipulating attention maps has proven effective for controlling diffusion-based generation and editing. Prompt-to-Prompt (P2P) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite> injects cross-attention maps from the source generation into the editing process to preserve spatial layout. Attend-and-Excite <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite> optimizes latents to ensure all subjects receive sufficient attention. Self-Guidance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite> leverages internal attention features for spatial control. MasaCtrl <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite> performs mutual self-attention control for consistent image synthesis. Perturbed-Attention Guidance (PAG) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite> improves sample quality by perturbing self-attention. Prior work on attention-based layout control <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite> has also demonstrated the effectiveness of manipulating attention losses for spatial guidance. Most recently, GRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite> decomposes Key projections into bias and delta components, rescaling them to control editing intensity. However, all these methods focus on either the Query-Key interaction (attention weights) or cross-attention maps, without exploiting the Value space. Our work is the first to identify and leverage the bias-delta structure in Value projections as a complementary control channel.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Diffusion Transformers.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architecture <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite> replaces the U-Net backbone <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite> with transformer blocks, enabling better scalability and performance. Subsequent work has scaled DiTs with rectified flow objectives <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite> and improved latent representations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>. Modern DiT-based editing models such as Qwen-Image-Edit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite> employ dual-stream architectures where text and image tokens are processed through joint multi-modal attention (MM-Attention) layers. In these architectures, the Key and Value projections of image tokens carry rich structural information about the source image, making them natural targets for editing control. Our DCAG framework is designed for this dual-stream MM-Attention setting but is applicable to any transformer-based diffusion model.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Preliminary</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Multi-Modal Attention in DiT</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Modern DiT-based image editing models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>, <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite> employ a dual-stream architecture with <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> transformer blocks (typically <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=60</annotation></semantics></math>). Each block contains a multi-modal attention (MM-Attention) layer that jointly processes text tokens <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}_{\text{txt}}\in\mathbb{R}^{S_{t}\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mtext>txt</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}_{\text{txt}}\in\mathbb{R}^{S_{t}\times D}</annotation></semantics></math> and image tokens <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}_{\text{img}}\in\mathbb{R}^{S_{i}\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mtext>img</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}_{\text{img}}\in\mathbb{R}^{S_{i}\times D}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are the sequence lengths and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> is the hidden dimension.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For each stream, separate Query, Key, and Value projections are computed:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle Q_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle Q_{s}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=W_{Q}^{s}\mathbf{X}_{s},\quad K_{s}=W_{K}^{s}\mathbf{X}_{s}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>s</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>K</mi><mi>s</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=W_{Q}^{s}\mathbf{X}_{s},\quad K_{s}=W_{K}^{s}\mathbf{X}_{s},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.E2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle V_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle V_{s}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=W_{V}^{s}\mathbf{X}_{s},\quad s\in\{\text{txt},\text{img}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>V</mi><mi>s</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mtext>txt</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>img</mtext><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=W_{V}^{s}\mathbf{X}_{s},\quad s\in\{\text{txt},\text{img}\}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">After applying rotary position embeddings (RoPE) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>]</cite> to <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, the streams are concatenated for joint attention:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=[Q_{\text{txt}};Q_{\text{img}}],\quad K=[K_{\text{txt}};K_{\text{img}}],\quad V=[V_{\text{txt}};V_{\text{img}}]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mtext>txt</mtext></msub><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mtext>img</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mtext>txt</mtext></msub><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mtext>img</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mtext>txt</mtext></msub><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mtext>img</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=[Q_{\text{txt}};Q_{\text{img}}],\quad K=[K_{\text{txt}};K_{\text{img}}],\quad V=[V_{\text{txt}};V_{\text{img}}]</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{h}</annotation></semantics></math> is the per-head dimension. The output is then split back into text and image streams for subsequent processing.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>The Bias-Delta Structure</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A key empirical observation, first noted for Key projections <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>, is that token embeddings in MM-Attention layers exhibit a pronounced clustering pattern. For the image Key tokens <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{K_{\text{img}}^{i}\}_{i=1}^{S_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mtext>img</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{K_{\text{img}}^{i}\}_{i=1}^{S_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> at any given layer, all tokens concentrate tightly around a shared bias vector:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\text{img}}^{i}=\underbrace{\bar{K}_{\text{img}}}_{\text{bias}}+\underbrace{(K_{\text{img}}^{i}-\bar{K}_{\text{img}})}_{\text{delta }\Delta K^{i}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mtext>img</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>bias</mtext></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mtext>img</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mtext>delta </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></munder></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\text{img}}^{i}=\underbrace{\bar{K}_{\text{img}}}_{\text{bias}}+\underbrace{(K_{\text{img}}^{i}-\bar{K}_{\text{img}})}_{\text{delta }\Delta K^{i}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{K}_{\text{img}}=\frac{1}{S_{i}}\sum_{i=1}^{S_{i}}K_{\text{img}}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msubsup><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mtext>img</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{K}_{\text{img}}=\frac{1}{S_{i}}\sum_{i=1}^{S_{i}}K_{\text{img}}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the token-wise mean. The bias component <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{K}_{\text{img}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{K}_{\text{img}}</annotation></semantics></math> encodes the layer’s overall editing behavior, while the delta component <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta K^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta K^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> captures token-specific content signals.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Our key finding:</span> We discover that this bias-delta structure is <em id="S3.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">not unique to Keys</em>. The Value projections exhibit the same clustering phenomenon:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{\text{img}}^{i}=\underbrace{\bar{V}_{\text{img}}}_{\text{bias}}+\underbrace{(V_{\text{img}}^{i}-\bar{V}_{\text{img}})}_{\text{delta }\Delta V^{i}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mtext>img</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>bias</mtext></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mtext>img</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mtext>delta </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></munder></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{\text{img}}^{i}=\underbrace{\bar{V}_{\text{img}}}_{\text{bias}}+\underbrace{(V_{\text{img}}^{i}-\bar{V}_{\text{img}})}_{\text{delta }\Delta V^{i}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">We provide empirical evidence for this observation through systematic profiling across all 60 layers and 24 denoising steps in <a href="#S5.SS5" title="5.5 Value-Space Profiling ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Sec.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a>. This discovery motivates our dual-channel approach: if both <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> have exploitable bias-delta structure, manipulating both channels should provide richer control than manipulating either alone.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Method: Dual-Channel Attention Guidance</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S4.F1" title="In 4 Method: Dual-Channel Attention Guidance ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> illustrates the overall DCAG framework. After RoPE encoding, DCAG independently rescales the Key and Value projections before the joint attention computation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18022v1/fig_method_overview.svg" id="S4.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/242;" width="685" height="242"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S4.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of DCAG. The Key channel controls attention routing (coarse, nonlinear) and the Value channel controls feature aggregation (fine, linear). Both channels apply bias-delta rescaling independently before the joint attention computation.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Dual-Channel Rescaling</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given the bias-delta decomposition of both Key and Value projections (<a href="#S3.E5" title="In 3.2 The Bias-Delta Structure ‣ 3 Preliminary ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqs.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> and <a href="#S3.E6" title="Equation 6 ‣ 3.2 The Bias-Delta Structure ‣ 3 Preliminary ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>), DCAG applies independent rescaling to each channel. For the image tokens at layer <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Key Channel (Attention Routing).</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{K}_{\text{img}}^{i}=\lambda_{k}\cdot\bar{K}_{\text{img}}+\delta_{k}\cdot\Delta K^{i}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{K}_{\text{img}}^{i}=\lambda_{k}\cdot\bar{K}_{\text{img}}+\delta_{k}\cdot\Delta K^{i}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Value Channel (Feature Aggregation).</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{V}_{\text{img}}^{i}=\lambda_{v}\cdot\bar{V}_{\text{img}}+\delta_{v}\cdot\Delta V^{i}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>img</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{V}_{\text{img}}^{i}=\lambda_{v}\cdot\bar{V}_{\text{img}}+\delta_{v}\cdot\Delta V^{i}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\lambda_{k},\delta_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\lambda_{k},\delta_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\lambda_{v},\delta_{v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\lambda_{v},\delta_{v})</annotation></semantics></math> are the bias and delta scales for each channel. Following prior findings that the delta scale is the primary control parameter <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>, we fix <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{k}=\lambda_{v}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{k}=\lambda_{v}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math> and focus on the delta scales <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})</annotation></semantics></math> as the two control knobs. When <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=\delta_{v}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=\delta_{v}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, DCAG reduces to the identity (no guidance). When <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, DCAG reduces to Key-only guidance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The rescaling is applied after RoPE and before the joint attention computation (<a href="#S3.E4" title="In 3.1 Multi-Modal Attention in DiT ‣ 3 Preliminary ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>), preserving positional encoding integrity. The complete procedure is summarized in <a href="#alg1" title="In Value Channel (Feature Aggregation). ‣ 4.1 Dual-Channel Rescaling ‣ 4 Method: Dual-Channel Attention Guidance ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> Dual-Channel Attention Guidance (DCAG)</figcaption>

<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Theoretical Analysis: Key vs. Value Channels</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To understand why the two channels provide complementary control, we analyze how perturbations in <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> affect the attention output. Consider a single query token <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> attending to image tokens. The attention output is:</p>
<table id="S4.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o=\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}\hat{V}^{i},\;\alpha_{i}=\frac{\exp(q^{\top}\hat{K}^{i}/\sqrt{d_{h}})}{\sum_{j}\exp(q^{\top}\hat{K}^{j}/\sqrt{d_{h}})}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo>/</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow><mo>/</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o=\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}\hat{V}^{i},\;\alpha_{i}=\frac{\exp(q^{\top}\hat{K}^{i}/\sqrt{d_{h}})}{\sum_{j}\exp(q^{\top}\hat{K}^{j}/\sqrt{d_{h}})}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Key Channel: Nonlinear Amplification.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Substituting the Key rescaling (<a href="#S4.E7" title="In Key Channel (Attention Routing). ‣ 4.1 Dual-Channel Rescaling ‣ 4 Method: Dual-Channel Attention Guidance ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>) with <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{k}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{k}=1</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\top}\hat{K}^{i}=q^{\top}\bar{K}+\delta_{k}\cdot q^{\top}\Delta K^{i}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\top}\hat{K}^{i}=q^{\top}\bar{K}+\delta_{k}\cdot q^{\top}\Delta K^{i}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The first term <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\top}\bar{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\top}\bar{K}</annotation></semantics></math> is shared across all tokens and cancels in the softmax normalization. The effective attention logit difference between tokens <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> is:</p>
<table id="S4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\top}\hat{K}^{i}-q^{\top}\hat{K}^{j}=\delta_{k}\cdot q^{\top}(\Delta K^{i}-\Delta K^{j})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\top}\hat{K}^{i}-q^{\top}\hat{K}^{j}=\delta_{k}\cdot q^{\top}(\Delta K^{i}-\Delta K^{j})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Through the softmax’s exponential function, this linear scaling of logit differences produces a <em id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">nonlinear, amplified</em> effect on the attention distribution. Increasing <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> sharpens the attention distribution, making it more peaked on tokens with high relevance. This is a <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">coarse control</span> mechanism—small changes in <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> can dramatically redistribute attention weights.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Value Channel: Linear Proportionality.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Substituting the Value rescaling (<a href="#S4.E8" title="In Value Channel (Feature Aggregation). ‣ 4.1 Dual-Channel Rescaling ‣ 4 Method: Dual-Channel Attention Guidance ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>) with <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{v}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{v}=1</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle o" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>o</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle o</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}(\bar{V}+\delta_{v}\cdot\Delta V^{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}(\bar{V}+\delta_{v}\cdot\Delta V^{i})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S4.E12"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\bar{V}+\delta_{v}\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}\Delta V^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\bar{V}+\delta_{v}\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}\Delta V^{i}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The output decomposes into a fixed bias term <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{V}</annotation></semantics></math> (independent of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>) and a scaled deviation term. The effect of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> on the output is <em id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">strictly linear</em>: doubling <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> doubles the deviation from the mean. This is a <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">fine control</span> mechanism—changes in <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> produce proportional, predictable effects on the output features.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Orthogonality.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Key channel modifies the attention weights <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\alpha_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\alpha_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math> (which tokens are attended to), while the Value channel modifies the features <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{V^{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{V^{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math> (what content is aggregated). These operate on different factors of the attention output <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o=\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}V^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o=\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}V^{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, making them functionally orthogonal. Increasing <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> amplifies per-token feature distinctiveness without changing the attention distribution, thereby preserving local details in non-edited regions.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>2D Parameter Space</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DCAG’s two control knobs <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})</annotation></semantics></math> span a 2D parameter plane. Each point in this plane corresponds to a specific editing-fidelity trade-off:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Origin</span> <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1.0,1.0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1.0,1.0)</annotation></semantics></math>: No guidance (baseline model behavior).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">K-axis</span> <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\delta_{k}&gt;1,1.0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\delta_{k}&gt;1,1.0)</annotation></semantics></math>: Key-only guidance (equivalent to prior methods).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">V-axis</span> <math id="S4.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1.0,\delta_{v}&gt;1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1.0,\delta_{v}&gt;1)</annotation></semantics></math>: Value-only guidance (novel).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Interior</span> <math id="S4.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\delta_{k}&gt;1,\delta_{v}&gt;1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\delta_{k}&gt;1,\delta_{v}&gt;1)</annotation></semantics></math>: Dual-channel guidance (DCAG).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A key property of this 2D space is the existence of <em id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">iso-fidelity contours</em>—curves along which the fidelity metric (e.g., LPIPS) remains approximately constant. Moving along such a contour trades off between Key-channel and Value-channel contributions while maintaining the same overall preservation level. This enables practitioners to find operating points that optimize editing quality at a desired fidelity level, which is impossible with single-channel methods.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Benchmark.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate on PIE-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>, a comprehensive image editing benchmark containing 700 images across 10 editing categories: Random, Change Object, Add Object, Delete Object, Change Attribute, Change Count, Change Background, Change Style, Change Action, and Change Position.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Metrics.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report four fidelity metrics measuring content preservation between source and edited images: LPIPS<math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> (perceptual distance), SSIM<math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite> (structural similarity), PSNR<math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math> (peak signal-to-noise ratio), and MSE<math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>. We additionally report CLIP-Score<math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite> to measure editing quality (semantic alignment between the edited image and the editing instruction).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Model.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All experiments use Qwen-Image-Edit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>, a 60-layer dual-stream DiT model. Inference uses 24 denoising steps, CFG scale 4.0, image resolution <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1024\times 1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024\times 1024</annotation></semantics></math>, and seed 42 for reproducibility.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Baselines.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare against: (1) <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">No Guidance</span>: the base model without any attention manipulation (<math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=\delta_{v}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=\delta_{v}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>); (2) <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GRAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>: the state-of-the-art Key-only attention guidance method, which rescales Key deltas with <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math> while keeping <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>. We evaluate GRAG at multiple <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> values to ensure fair comparison.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Main Results</h3>

<td id="S5.T1.9.11.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.9.11.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">1742</span></td></tr>

<td id="S5.T1.9.13.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.9.13.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">1.20</span></td>

<td id="S5.T1.9.13.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.9.13.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">21.91</span></td>
<td id="S5.T1.9.13.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.9.13.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">1060</span></td></tr>

<td id="S5.T1.9.15.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.9.15.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.3126</span></td>
