<td id="S5.T1.9.15.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S5.T1.9.15.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">3497</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Key observations:</p>
<ul id="S5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Attention guidance dramatically improves fidelity.</span> The No Guidance baseline (LPIPS = 0.3523) confirms that the base model produces significant unintended modifications. GRAG (<math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10</annotation></semantics></math>) reduces LPIPS by 26.5% to 0.2588, and DCAG (<math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10,\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10,\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15</annotation></semantics></math>) further reduces it by 27.8% to 0.2542.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DCAG improves upon K-only guidance.</span> At <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=1.10</annotation></semantics></math>, adding Value-channel guidance monotonically improves LPIPS from 0.2588 (<math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}\!=\!1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}\!=\!1.0</annotation></semantics></math>) to 0.2542 (<math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15</annotation></semantics></math>), a 1.8% reduction. The sweet spot is <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}=1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}=1.15</annotation></semantics></math>; further increasing to <math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}=1.20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}=1.20</annotation></semantics></math> causes slight regression (0.2546), indicating a saturation effect.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">V-channel effect is near-monotonic with saturation.</span> Across the range <math id="S5.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}\in[1.0,1.15]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}\in[1.0,1.15]</annotation></semantics></math>, all four fidelity metrics improve monotonically. Beyond 1.15, LPIPS and SSIM slightly regress while PSNR continues to decrease, suggesting the Value-channel amplification begins to distort fine-grained features.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">K-channel is dominant.</span> Reducing <math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> from 1.10 to 1.05 (with <math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}=1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}=1.10</annotation></semantics></math>) causes a 20.8% LPIPS degradation, far exceeding the 1.8% improvement from the full V-channel range. This confirms the theoretical prediction: the Key channel (nonlinear softmax amplification) has a much stronger effect than the Value channel (linear scaling).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Diminishing V-channel returns at higher <math id="S5.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span> At <math id="S5.I1.i5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=1.15</annotation></semantics></math>, adding <math id="S5.I1.i5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}=1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}=1.15</annotation></semantics></math> yields only 0.9% LPIPS improvement (0.1991<math id="S5.I1.i5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math>0.1974), with SSIM and PSNR slightly decreasing. This suggests that stronger Key-channel guidance already captures most of the achievable fidelity gain, leaving less room for Value-channel contribution.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Per-Category Analysis</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">

</div>

<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The improvement pattern reveals an important insight about the Value channel’s operating characteristics:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Broad improvement at moderate <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span> At <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=1.10</annotation></semantics></math>, DCAG improves 8 out of 10 categories. The largest gains appear in Delete Object (<math id="S5.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>4.3%), Change Background (<math id="S5.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>4.2%), and Change Style (<math id="S5.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>3.7%). These categories involve either localized editing regions or texture-level changes where amplifying per-token Value distinctiveness directly reduces feature mixing in non-edited areas.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Interaction with <math id="S5.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> level.</span> At <math id="S5.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=1.15</annotation></semantics></math>, the per-category pattern shifts: Random (<math id="S5.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>3.0%), Change Object (<math id="S5.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>3.1%), and Change Position (<math id="S5.SS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>2.4%) still improve, but Add Object (<math id="S5.SS3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>11.2%) and Change Style (<math id="S5.SS3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>7.6%) regress. This suggests that at higher Key-channel guidance, the attention routing already strongly preserves non-edited regions, and additional Value amplification can over-sharpen features in categories with small editing footprints.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Practical implication.</span> The Value channel is most effective as a complement to moderate Key-channel guidance (<math id="S5.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\approx 1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\approx 1.10</annotation></semantics></math>), where it provides consistent improvement across nearly all categories. At stronger Key guidance, the Value channel should be used conservatively or omitted.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4 </span>Ablation: V-Channel Saturation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S5.T3" title="In 5.4 Ablation: V-Channel Saturation ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tab.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows the effect of sweeping <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> at fixed <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=1.10</annotation></semantics></math>, revealing the Value channel’s saturation behavior.</p>
</div>

<div id="S5.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The saturation at <math id="S5.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}\approx 1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}\approx 1.15</annotation></semantics></math> is consistent with the linear nature of the Value channel: beyond a certain amplification, the per-token deviations <math id="S5.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta V^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta V^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> become large enough to distort the feature content rather than sharpen it. This contrasts with the Key channel, where the nonlinear softmax amplification allows a wider effective range before saturation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18022v1/fig_v_sweep.svg" id="S5.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:514/336;" width="514" height="336"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S5.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">V-channel sweep at fixed <math id="S5.F2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=1.10</annotation></semantics></math>. LPIPS (blue, left axis) improves monotonically up to <math id="S5.F2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}=1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}=1.15</annotation></semantics></math>, then saturates. SSIM (red, right axis) follows the same pattern. The sweet spot at <math id="S5.F2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}\approx 1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}\approx 1.15</annotation></semantics></math> reflects the linear nature of the Value channel.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S5.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18022v1/fig_per_category.svg" id="S5.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/398;" width="685" height="398"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S5.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Per-category LPIPS comparison between K-only (<math id="S5.F3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.128em">=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10</annotation></semantics></math>) and DCAG (<math id="S5.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10,\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.128em">=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10,\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15</annotation></semantics></math>). Top: absolute LPIPS values. Bottom: relative improvement (%). DCAG improves 8 out of 10 categories, with the largest gains in Delete Object (<math id="S5.F3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>4.3%) and Change Background (<math id="S5.F3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>4.2%).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5 </span>Value-Space Profiling</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To empirically validate that the bias-delta structure exists in the Value space, we profile both Key and Value projections across all 60 layers and 24 denoising steps. For each space <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\{K,V\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\{K,V\}</annotation></semantics></math>, layer <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>, and step <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute the delta-to-bias ratio:</p>
<table id="S5.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{X}^{(l,t)}=\frac{\text{mean}_{i}\|X^{i}-\bar{X}\|_{2}}{\|\bar{X}\|_{2}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mtext>mean</mtext><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{X}^{(l,t)}=\frac{\text{mean}_{i}\|X^{i}-\bar{X}\|_{2}}{\|\bar{X}\|_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S5.F4" title="In 5.5 Value-Space Profiling ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> presents the ratio heatmaps for both spaces. The results provide strong evidence for our hypothesis:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S5.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Value space exhibits pervasive delta structure.</span> The delta-to-bias ratio is significantly greater than zero across all 1440 layer-step combinations (100%), with a mean ratio of 2.45. This confirms that Value tokens cluster around a layer-specific bias with meaningful per-token deviations—the prerequisite for our rescaling approach.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Value deltas are relatively stronger than Key deltas.</span> The mean V-ratio (2.45) exceeds the mean K-ratio (1.79) by a factor of 1.37<math id="S5.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating that Value space actually has proportionally larger deviations from the bias. This suggests Value-space manipulation has substantial room for effect.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">K and V structures are largely independent.</span> The Pearson correlation between K-ratio and V-ratio across all layer-step pairs is <math id="S5.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=-0.17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.17</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=-0.17</annotation></semantics></math>, confirming that the two spaces carry largely orthogonal structural information. This supports the theoretical prediction that the two channels provide complementary control.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18022v1/fig_kv_profiling.png" id="S5.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:685/263;" width="685" height="263" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S5.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Delta-to-bias ratio heatmaps across 60 layers (x-axis) and 24 denoising steps (y-axis). Left: Key space. Right: Value space. Both spaces exhibit pervasive bias-delta structure, with Value ratios (mean 2.45) consistently higher than Key ratios (mean 1.79). The weak correlation (<math id="S5.F4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=-0.17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.17</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=-0.17</annotation></semantics></math>) between the two confirms their structural independence.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.6 </span>Qualitative Comparison</h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S5.F5" title="In 5.6 Qualitative Comparison ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Dual-Channel Attention Guidance for Training-Free Image Editing Control in Diffusion Transformers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> presents qualitative comparisons across five editing categories. For each example, we show the source image, K-only guidance (<math id="S5.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10</annotation></semantics></math>), DCAG (<math id="S5.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10,\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10,\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15</annotation></semantics></math>), and stronger K-only guidance (<math id="S5.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.15</annotation></semantics></math>) for reference.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18022v1/fig_qualitative.png" id="S5.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:685/865;" width="685" height="865" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S5.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Qualitative comparison across editing categories. DCAG (<math id="S5.F5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10,\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.128em">=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10,\delta_{v}\!=\!1.15</annotation></semantics></math>) better preserves non-edited regions compared to K-only (<math id="S5.F5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.128em">=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.10</annotation></semantics></math>), while maintaining editing quality. K-only (<math id="S5.F5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\!=\!1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.128em">=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\!=\!1.15</annotation></semantics></math>) achieves higher fidelity but at the cost of reduced editing strength.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Discussion and Conclusion</h2>

<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Why Dual-Channel Outperforms Single-Channel.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Key and Value channels operate on different factors of the attention output <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o=\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}V^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o=\sum_{i}\alpha_{i}V^{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. Key-channel guidance modifies the weights <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\alpha_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\alpha_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, redistributing attention across tokens. Value-channel guidance modifies the features <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{V^{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{V^{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, adjusting what content each token contributes. Because these are multiplicative factors, their effects compose rather than interfere. DCAG exploits this composability to achieve fidelity improvements that are inaccessible to either channel alone.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Practical Guidelines.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Based on our experiments, we recommend the following guidelines for practitioners:</p>
<ul id="S6.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Use <math id="S6.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=1.10,\delta_{v}=1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=1.10,\delta_{v}=1.15</annotation></semantics></math> as the default configuration (best overall fidelity).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At moderate Key guidance (<math id="S6.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\approx 1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\approx 1.10</annotation></semantics></math>), the Value channel improves nearly all edit types; <math id="S6.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}\in[1.05,1.15]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1.05</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}\in[1.05,1.15]</annotation></semantics></math> is the effective range.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At stronger Key guidance (<math id="S6.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}\geq 1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}\geq 1.15</annotation></semantics></math>), use the Value channel conservatively (<math id="S6.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}\leq 1.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>1.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}\leq 1.05</annotation></semantics></math>) or omit it, as some categories may regress.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For localized edits (delete/add objects, change background), <math id="S6.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> provides the most benefit.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For global edits (change action/position), <math id="S6.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> has limited effect; focus on <math id="S6.I1.i5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Value channel saturates at <math id="S6.I1.i6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{v}\approx 1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{v}\approx 1.15</annotation></semantics></math>; beyond this, features begin to distort rather than sharpen.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Limitations.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Value channel’s effect is inherently milder than the Key channel due to its linear nature. While this makes it predictable and safe (no risk of artifacts), the overall improvement is modest (1.8% LPIPS at best). Furthermore, the Value channel exhibits diminishing returns at higher <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>: at <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=1.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=1.15</annotation></semantics></math>, the improvement drops to 0.9% and some categories regress. This interaction between channels suggests that the two are not fully independent in practice—strong Key-channel guidance already captures most achievable fidelity gains, leaving less room for Value-channel contribution. Our current evaluation focuses on fidelity metrics; a comprehensive study of editing quality trade-offs (e.g., via CLIP-Score) across the 2D parameter space remains future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Future Directions.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Several extensions are worth exploring: (1) <em id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Spatially-adaptive DCAG</em>, where <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\delta_{k},\delta_{v})</annotation></semantics></math> vary per-token based on edit relevance, similar to mask-guided approaches <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>, <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>; (2) <em id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Query-space guidance</em>, extending the bias-delta framework to the third projection; (3) <em id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Video editing</em>, where temporal consistency adds another dimension to the control problem; (4) integration with identity-preserving generation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite> for controlled personalized editing.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Conclusion.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented Dual-Channel Attention Guidance (DCAG), a training-free framework for fine-grained image editing control in Diffusion Transformers. By discovering and exploiting the bias-delta structure in both Key and Value projections, DCAG provides a 2D parameter space that enables more precise editing-fidelity trade-offs than single-channel methods. Our theoretical analysis reveals the complementary nature of the two channels—Key for coarse nonlinear control, Value for fine linear control—and extensive experiments on PIE-Bench validate consistent improvements across diverse editing categories.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="Sx1.SSx4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Data Availability</h3>

<div id="Sx1.SSx4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.SSx4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The datasets used in this study are available in the PIE-Bench repository (<a href="https://github.com/timothybrooks/instruct-pix2pix" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/timothybrooks/instruct-pix2pix</a>). The pre-trained base model (Qwen-Image-Edit) used in this study is publicly available from HuggingFace (<a href="https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit</a>). The evaluation metrics rely on publicly available implementations of LPIPS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>, SSIM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>, and CLIP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
